category.title: Hashing & Hash Tables
category.description: Hash maps, hash sets, frequency maps, two-sum lookups, and prefix sum hashing.

algorithms.title: Hash Table Architecture & Collision Resolution
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(1) Average Lookup/Insert, O(N) Worst Case
algorithms.summary: Core hash table concepts including hash functions, load factor α = N/M, rehashing, and collision resolution techniques (Chaining vs. Open Addressing).
explanation: Hash Function: Maps arbitrary keys (strings, numbers, objects) to an integer index within an array bucket of size M.
Load Factor (α = N/M): Ratio of stored items N to bucket size M. When α exceeds a threshold (~0.75), Rehashing creates a 2x larger table and re-maps all keys.
Separate Chaining: Each bucket holds a Linked List or BST of colliding key-value pairs.
Open Addressing: Resolves collisions within the main array using Linear Probing (index + i), Quadratic Probing (index + i²), or Double Hashing (index + i * hash2(key)).

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Enables expected constant-time O(1) key-value insertion, deletion, and lookup.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When instant O(1) data retrieval by unique key is required.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Database indexing, in-memory caches (Redis/Memcached), compiler symbol tables, language dictionaries.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Provides expected O(1) lookup speed compared to O(log N) in BSTs or O(N) in linear arrays.

algorithms.title: Frequency Map & Anagram Pattern
algorithms.spaceComplexity: O(K) where K is alphabet size (e.g. 26 characters)
algorithms.summary: Uses a Hash Map or fixed frequency array to count element occurrences and verify Anagram equivalence.
explanation: Two strings s and t are Anagrams if they contain the exact same character frequencies.
Count character frequencies of s into a Hash Map (+1 for each char).
Decrement frequency counts using string t (-1 for each char).
If all HashMap counts return to 0, s and t are valid anagrams.

traceSteps: Strings are valid anagrams. Return True.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Verifies structural equivalence and permutation matches in linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When checking for anagrams, character counts, or word frequency matches.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Plagiarism detectors, search query spell checkers, word game engines.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces O(N log N) string sorting with O(N) linear hash counting.

algorithms.title: Majority Element Pattern (HashMap & Boyer-Moore)
algorithms.spaceComplexity: O(N) with HashMap or O(1) with Boyer-Moore Voting
algorithms.summary: Finds the majority element that appears more than ⌊N/2⌋ times using Hash Map counting or Boyer-Moore Voting algorithm.
explanation: HashMap Approach: Store frequency count of each element. If `count[x] > N/2`, return `x`.
Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm (O(1) Space): Maintain candidate and count.
Iterate through array. If count is 0, pick current element as candidate.
Increment count if num == candidate, else decrement count.
The surviving candidate is guaranteed to be the majority element.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Identifies the dominant majority element in linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding elements occurring more than N/2 (or N/3) times.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Consensus algorithms, streaming analytics, voting systems.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Boyer-Moore achieves O(N) time with O(1) space.

algorithms.title: Two Sum & Duplicate Detection Lookup Pattern
algorithms.summary: Solves Two Sum and Duplicate Detection by maintaining a Hash Map/Set of visited elements to perform O(1) complement lookups.
explanation: For each element `x` at index `i`, calculate required complement `target - x`.
Check if `target - x` exists in Hash Map.
If found: Return `[map[target - x], i]` immediately.
If not found: Store `map[x] = i` and continue single-pass iteration.

traceSteps: i = 0 (val 2): diff = 9 - 2 = 7. Not in map. Store seen[2] = 0.
i = 1 (val 7): diff = 9 - 7 = 2. Found in map at index 0!

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds element pairs meeting a target condition in single-pass linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When searching for complement pairs, duplicates, or target sums in unsorted arrays.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Transaction matching, database join optimization, deduplication pipelines.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Reduces O(N²) nested loop checks to single-pass O(N) time using O(1) hash lookups.

algorithms.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence (HashSet O(N))
algorithms.summary: Finds the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence in an unsorted array in linear O(N) time.
explanation: Insert all numbers into a HashSet.
Iterate through numbers in HashSet.
Check if `num - 1` exists in HashSet. If `num - 1` exists, `num` is NOT the start of a sequence (skip it).
If `num - 1` does NOT exist, `num` is the START of a consecutive sequence!
Count length by iteratively checking `num + 1`, `num + 2`, etc., in the HashSet. Update max length.

traceSteps: Inspect 100: (99 not in set) -> chain: [100]. length=1.
Inspect 200: (199 not in set) -> chain: [200]. length=1.
Inspect 1: (0 not in set) -> sequence start! Count 1, 2, 3, 4. length=4.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds the longest contiguous numerical range without sorting the array.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding consecutive sequences in unsorted data under O(N) time constraint.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Data gap analysis, consecutive log session detection, interval grouping.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces O(N log N) sorting with linear O(N) set lookups by only starting chains at true sequence boundaries.

algorithms.title: Subarray Sum Equals K (Prefix Sum + HashMap)
algorithms.summary: Finds total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals K using Prefix Sum hashing.
explanation: Maintain `curr_prefix_sum` while iterating through array.
Key Insight: If `curr_prefix_sum - K` was seen previously in our prefix sum map, then the subarray between that previous index and current index sums to K!
Maintain HashMap `map[prefix_sum] = frequency`.
Initialize `map[0] = 1` (handles subarrays starting at index 0).
At each step: `count += map[curr_prefix_sum - K]`, then increment `map[curr_prefix_sum] += 1`.

traceSteps: Num 1: curr_sum = 1. diff = 1 - 2 = -1 (not in map). map = {0:1, 1:1}.
Num 1: curr_sum = 2. diff = 2 - 2 = 0 (found in map, val=1!). count = 1. map = {0:1, 1:1, 2:1}.
Num 1: curr_sum = 3. diff = 3 - 2 = 1 (found in map, val=1!). count = 2. map = {0:1, 1:1, 2:1, 3:1}.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Counts continuous range subarrays matching a target sum K.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When counting continuous subarrays with sum K in arrays containing positive & negative integers.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Financial ledger sub-transaction matching, signal processing window detection.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Reduces O(N²) range sum checks to single-pass O(N) using HashMap lookup.

algorithms.title: Longest Subarray with Sum K
algorithms.summary: Finds the maximum length of a continuous subarray that sums to K using Prefix Sum first-occurrence HashMap tracking.
explanation: Maintain prefix sum `curr_sum` and a HashMap storing `first_occurrence[prefix_sum] = index`.
If `curr_sum == K`: max_len = max(max_len, i + 1).
If `(curr_sum - K)` exists in HashMap: max_len = max(max_len, i - first_occurrence[curr_sum - K]).
Only store `first_occurrence` when `curr_sum` is seen for the FIRST time to maximize window length.

traceSteps: i=3 (val 7): sum=24. diff = 24 - 15 = 9 (not in map). first_occ[24]=3.
i=4 (val 1): sum=25. diff = 25 - 15 = 10 (found at idx 0!). len = 4 - 0 = 4. max_len = 4.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximum contiguous window length matching target sum K.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding maximum length subarray summing to K in arrays with negative/positive numbers.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Maximum span detection in audio/sensor signals, financial maximum gain windows.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Storing first occurrence guarantees maximum possible subarray width.

algorithms.title: Zero-Sum Subarray Detection & Length
algorithms.summary: Detects if a zero-sum subarray exists and finds its maximum length using prefix sum repetition property.
explanation: Mathematical Property: Subarray [i...j] sums to 0 if and only if `prefixSum[j] == prefixSum[i-1]`.
Iterate through array while maintaining running `prefix_sum`.
If `prefix_sum == 0` or `prefix_sum` was seen previously in HashSet/HashMap, a zero-sum subarray exists!
To find maximum length: store `first_occurrence[prefix_sum] = index` and calculate `i - first_occurrence[prefix_sum]`.

traceSteps: i=5 (7): sum=15 (seen at idx 0!). len = 5 - 0 = 5. max_len = 5.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Detects zero-sum sub-ranges or balanced net zero fluctuations.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When checking if a sequence contains any zero-sum window or longest zero-sum sub-array.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Net zero financial balance calculations, game score reset detection.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Prefix sum repetition detection yields exact O(N) performance.

algorithms.title: Contiguous Array with Equal 0s and 1s
algorithms.summary: Finds the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s by transforming 0s to -1s.
explanation: Transformation trick: Treat every '0' as '-1' and every '1' as '+1'.
An equal number of 0s and 1s in a subarray now means the sum of transformed elements equals 0!
Maintain running count: `curr_sum += 1` if num == 1 else `curr_sum -= 1`.
Use HashMap to store `first_occurrence[curr_sum] = index` initialized with `{0: -1}`.
If `curr_sum` repeats at index `i`, max_len = max(max_len, i - first_occurrence[curr_sum]).

traceSteps: i=3 (val +1): sum = 0 (seen at idx -1!). len = 3 - (-1) = 4. max_len = 4.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximum length subarray with balanced binary counts.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When checking for equal counts of two binary states (0 vs 1, win vs loss, true vs false).
wAnswers.whereUsed: Binary signal balance analyzers, fair A/B testing window calculations.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Transforming 0 to -1 converts the problem to Zero-Sum Subarray in single-pass O(N) time.
